comparisons.peer_topic: General Litigation and Regulatory Risk Exposure
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel is subject to risks from various litigation and regulatory matters, including stockholder, competition, IP, and labor issues. Adverse rulings can result in material adverse impacts, monetary damages, fines, or injunctions, regardless of the outcome, proceedings are costly and disruptive.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and INTC disclose that legal and regulatory proceedings impose significant management burdens and financial costs, and that adverse outcomes can materially harm business operations. QCOM specifically links these legal costs and potential revenue impacts to a forced reduction in R&D spending, which impairs technology leadership. INTC describes the proceedings as 'costly, time-consuming, disruptive... and distracting to management' and notes that adverse rulings can result in injunctions stopping manufacturing or sales, but does not explicitly mention the cascading effect on R&D budget cuts or capital return programs as QCOM does.

sentences.text: The occurrence of any of the above could have a material adverse effect on our business, revenues, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition, and our stock price could decline, possibly significantly, in which case we may have to significantly cut costs and other uses of cash, including in research and development, significantly impairing our ability to maintain product and technology leadership and invest in next generation technologies.

Further, depending on the breadth and severity of the circumstances above, we may have to reduce, suspend or eliminate our capital return programs, and our ability to timely pay our indebtedness may be impacted.
An unfavorable outcome can result in a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
Regardless of the outcome, litigation and regulatory proceedings can be costly, time-consuming, disruptive to our operations, harmful to our reputation, and distracting to management.
